A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Koopmans's model of hydroelectric storage has been extended to the case of competitive profit maximization with time-dependent electricity prices.

the hydroelectric problem is best formulated as a profit maximization problem, and that the Koopmans solution is a special case of the profit solution, with a particular choice of the electricity market price ( p ).

the hydroelectric storage problem can be treated in a manner that is both more general and more specific than Koopmans's original treatment, and that it is also more realistic in the sense that it is based on competitive market pricing.

the marginal value of water storage capacity is the total positive variation in the shadow price of water over the cycle, and the marginal value of a turbine is the total positive change in the shadow price over the cycle minus the shadow price at the end of the cycle.
